pain_point: A confirmed event may become uneditable by its requester, forcing an email handoff for changes
severity_rationale: Adds queue time and duplicate communication after confirmation
source_context: Brown University 25Live FAQ says requesters cannot edit confirmed events and must email the scheduling office
prevalence_limitations: One institution's permissions and workflow configuration; not proof of product-wide behavior

pain_point: Large institutional datasets can make searches slow; institutional pages also document freezes or stale-state troubleshooting
severity_rationale: Latency and freezing can interrupt routine room discovery and submission; refresh can discard unsaved wizard data
source_context: Brown says searches may take time because nine years of data are retained; Humboldt documents slow/freezing behavior; Virginia warns that refresh can clear unsaved information
prevalence_limitations: Institution-specific support pages do not quantify frequency and may reflect local configuration browser or data volume

pain_point: Recurring and irregular meeting-pattern events can fail to convert cleanly during a platform migration and require manual recreation
severity_rationale: Manual reconstruction creates launch workload and a risk of missing occurrences
source_context: University of Minnesota migration guidance from Astra Schedule to 25Live identifies recurring or multiple meeting-pattern events as difficult to convert
prevalence_limitations: One institution and one migration path; not evidence of normal post-launch operation

pain_point: Room identifiers can disagree across scheduling records floorplans and facilities master data
affected_role: Event requesters schedulers and facilities staff
severity_rationale: Mismatched labels can send users to the wrong place and undermine trust in availability data
source_context: University of Alaska Anchorage warns that numbers outside rooms may not match floorplans or facilities master data
prevalence_limitations: One institution; the root problem is cross-system data governance rather than necessarily 25Live

pain_point: Administrators report a dated and confusing interface, weak mobile usability and multi-step status handling
affected_role: Schedulers system administrators and event staff
severity_rationale: Usability friction compounds in high-volume scheduling and makes training more important
source_context: Capterra reviewers in higher education independently mention a dated interface limited mobile usefulness and confusing status labels
prevalence_limitations: Small self-selected review sample; reviews span versions and include both invited and organic participation

pain_point: Support and service charges can be hard to navigate, while SIS connector behavior varies by platform
severity_rationale: Ambiguous service boundaries and one-way synchronization can increase manual reconciliation and implementation cost
evidence_type: user reviews and vendor technical documentation
source_context: A 2025 higher-ed Capterra reviewer describes confusing charges and frustrating support; EMS documentation says the current Workday integration pulls data into EMS but does not synchronize back
prevalence_limitations: Single review for service complaints; Workday limitation should not be generalized to Banner or other connectors

pain_point: Some scheduling views can omit prerequisite corequisite and restriction context, while an analytics calculation can misstate course size
severity_rationale: Missing rule context can allow avoidable review loops; inaccurate denominators weaken decisions about rooms and capacity
source_context: Drew University lists known issues: prerequisite/corequisite/restriction data are not viewable in Scheduling and analytics average course size is not entirely accurate
prevalence_limitations: One institution's configuration and point-in-time known-issue page; resolution status can change

pain_point: A feature-rich scheduling workspace can overwhelm new users
severity_rationale: Training and progressive disclosure matter when occasional users face dense schedule data
source_context: Verified Assistant Registrar review on G2 says newer users may feel overwhelmed by the amount of information
prevalence_limitations: Single organic review; no prevalence estimate

pain_point: Infrequent users report a steep learning curve and too many clicks for simple changes
affected_role: Facility booking specialists project managers and occasional schedulers
severity_rationale: Complexity makes decentralized adoption and staff turnover harder
source_context: Two verified G2 reviewers describe the system as not always intuitive or overwhelming and say simple changes take more clicks
prevalence_limitations: Two self-selected reviews; one was G2-invited and AI-translated

pain_point: Spreadsheet and email-based schedule collection creates duplicate work version risk delays and weak analytical visibility
affected_role: Registrar academic departments and institutional research
workflow: Department schedule submission and central consolidation
severity_rationale: These failures affect the authoritative class schedule and propagate into registration room assignment and reporting
source_context: Villanova describes its pre-Coursedog process as Excel files exchanged by email with error duplicate-work delay and analysis risks
prevalence_limitations: One institution's transformation rationale; vendor selection context may emphasize shortcomings

pain_point: Central room data and software do not resolve decentralized authority policy and departmental reluctance to share space
affected_role: Registrar facilities departments and academic leaders
severity_rationale: A technically available room remains unusable to the institution if governance ownership or release rules block it
source_context: EDUCAUSE's enterprise application analysis emphasizes cross-stakeholder policy and reluctance around centralized room scheduling
prevalence_limitations: Older cross-institution research; organizational dynamics remain relevant but current prevalence was not measured here

pain_point: Course access problems may be caused by demand conflict and governance choices even when a scheduling tool exists
affected_role: Students registrars department chairs and advisors
workflow: Course offering design and conflict resolution
severity_rationale: A required-course conflict or missing section can delay progress and cannot be solved by room booking alone
source_context: AASCU's student-centered scheduling initiative reports that authority habits and governance are recurring barriers and that targeted section or conflict changes can matter
prevalence_limitations: Program evidence covers participating public regional institutions; vendor Ad Astra is a program partner and generalized prevalence should not be inferred

pain_point: Reserved-room utilization can be mistaken for actual occupancy, producing false confidence about space use
affected_role: Facilities analysts registrar and campus planners
severity_rationale: Scheduling records measure intended use; decisions about operating costs or capital require clarity about whether people actually occupied the room
source_context: University of Minnesota separates time utilization from projected and actual seat utilization; Microsoft Places explains that reservations show intended use while check-ins or sensors show observed occupancy
prevalence_limitations: Definitions establish measurement limits but do not estimate the size of the error at any institution

pain_point: Student organizations can face late booking windows or availability-loading failures that make planning uncertain
severity_rationale: Short lead time can block speakers equipment and attendance planning
source_context: A Berkeley student-club post reports that requests opened only three weeks ahead and rooms did not load
prevalence_limitations: Single anecdote; the booking window may be university policy and the loading issue was not independently diagnosed
